On VTES-L, Pierre TRAN-VAN writes:

> A humble question, as I was reading a Web article about Rush decks :
>
> Can Torn signpost be combined with Undead Strength to strike for 5
> damage at (at superior)? I thought no, since the 3 damage from Torn
> Signpost is done 'as a strike'.

If it were played as the VTES card text reads, you'd be right.
But it has been ruled/errata'ed to play as the Jyhad text reads -
that is, it sets the vampire's hand damage (his strength) to some
new amount - 2 or 3 depending on the level of the discipline.
[TOM 06-MAR-96]

I'll put this on the list for RT review to see if there's any
reason to keep this errata.

--

LSJ wrote:
"If it were played as the VTES card text reads, you'd be right.
But it has been ruled/errata'ed to play as the Jyhad text reads -
that is, it sets the vampire's hand damage (his strength) to some
new amount - 2 or 3 depending on the level of the discipline.
[TOM 06-MAR-96]

I'll put this on the list for RT review to see if there's any
reason to keep this errata."

Umm, what?

The text on the VTES version of Torn Signpost is poorly worded, ambigious, and
in no way clearly indicates that the VTES version of TS works any different
than the Jyhad version. The errata on this card is far more of a clarification
than a rules change.

Next, what possible reason is there to make Torn Signpost work differently than
it currently does. It is the very basis of Potence combat. Changing TS to
some sort of misbegotten strike card would be like changing Govern the
Unaligned to some sort of card where you could not play additional bleed
modifiers on top of it, or changing Enhanced Senses into some card that does
not allow the addition of further intercept. It changes the fundimentals of
the Potence discipline, and hinders it in an unacceptable fashion.

Add to this that it would make the fairly rare Fists of Death into such a _far_
superior card than Torn Signpost as to make it a complete necessity for a
Potence combat deck, making such decks even _more_ dependent on Rare cards than
they already are. Currently, Potence combat decks, if they wish to be as
effective as comparative Bleed or Vote decks need an inordinate number of Rare
cards, as opposed to the aforementioned Bleed or Vote decks, that thrive solely
on commons. Turning Torn Signpost into the card that is possibly implied by
the incredibly poorly written VTES text is to doom the Potence combat deck to a
fate of only being playable by a a smaller pool of players than it allready is.

The possibility of changing Torn Signpost into some sort of strike card is in
no way a good idea, and would be nothing but a detriment to the game as a
whole.

The text of the VTES version clearly gives the user a new option for
a strike - that is, one that will inflict 2 or 3 hand damage. This
is not ambiguous. If you believe that it was an attempt to set the
users hand damage to some new amount, then it is certainly poorly
worded, for it fails to do that altogether.

It does indeed seem that the designers were attempting to clarify the
Jyhad version - clarify it so that it was clear that Torn Signpost was
granting a strike option, not resetting the vampire's strength. (Which
is one way of reading the original Jyhad text).

> Next, what possible reason is there to make Torn Signpost work differently than
> it currently does.

Original intent would be a good reason (if it is true that original
intent is not the same as the current errata, which I'm not saying
is the case - just that it would be a reason to change).

> [many arguments deleted]

Woah. First, arguing with such an emotional stance isn't very
productive.

Second, I agree that potence decks (and straight combat decks in
general) are harder to win with than bleed or vote decks. That's
due to the nature of combat (in that it doesn't attack your prey's
pool directly). Changing TS did't change that, and removing the
errata won't change it. You have to take that fact into consideration
when building a deck. A pure quietus deck won't win much, either.

If the errata to the VTES card was for game balance or to preserve
original intent, then it should stay. As it is, though, it was
issued (by Tom) without reference to either of these things - indeed
without reference to the fact that it was errata at all. That is
why it is on the list for the RT to review.

Arguments against the errata: original card text could be read the
way the VTES clearly reads. Current errata makes TS much more
useful than Fists of Death - and so useful that it is a "staple"
of any combat deck, in some people's opinion (not mine).

Arguments for the errata: original card text could be read the way the
errata says, and the current errata is the current errata, and it's
not a broken card with the errata.

I'm not opposed to keeping the errata. But it is still an issue
that should be reviewed by the RT.

LSJ wrote:
"The text of the VTES version clearly gives the user a new option for
a strike - that is, one that will inflict 2 or 3 hand damage. This
is not ambiguous. If you believe that it was an attempt to set the
users hand damage to some new amount, then it is certainly poorly
worded, for it fails to do that altogether."

But it is not framed in such a way that this makes sense. All other Strike
cards use the template of "Strike:X". The VTES text does not convey this in
any way, nor is it clear as to what it means. It is pretty much the only card
in the set that uses such bizzare wording, and there is no precident set to
clarify such wording. It is worded in such a way to imply two different
things, and is clear about neither.

"It does indeed seem that the designers were attempting to clarify the
Jyhad version - clarify it so that it was clear that Torn Signpost was
granting a strike option, not resetting the vampire's strength. (Which
is one way of reading the original Jyhad text)."

I fail to see how the Jyhad version could be read this way. It very clearly
says "Vampire does 2 hand damage for the remainder of combat". This is pretty
clear.

"Original intent would be a good reason (if it is true that original
intent is not the same as the current errata, which I'm not saying
is the case - just that it would be a reason to change)."

The original intent is pretty clear--it gives a vampire 2 (or 3) hand damage.
To attempt to read into the card that it is some sort of Strike option (thereby
not allowing other strike options) is to read into the text something that is
completely absent.

"Woah. First, arguing with such an emotional stance isn't very
productive."

What emotional stance was I arguing from that wasn't productive? I presented a
threefold (twofold?) succinct argument as to why it would be foolish to change
Torn Signpost. That is all. No yelling, name calling, whining, anything of
the sort. Very straight forward.

"Changing TS did't change that, and removing the
errata won't change it. You have to take that fact into consideration
when building a deck. A pure quietus deck won't win much, either."

As you point out, Torn Signpost is often considered a basic element of a
Potence deck. Changing it in such a way to reduce this function, again, is
like arbirtarily changing all the Govern the Unaligned (Legal Manipulations,
Computer Hacking, whatever) type cards to prevent Bleed modifiers from being
played on them--you'll have to take it into consideration when building a deck.
This is true of any change. It doesn't however, make it necessarily a good
idea.

"Arguments against the errata: original card text could be read the
way the VTES clearly reads. Current errata makes TS much more
useful than Fists of Death - and so useful that it is a "staple"
of any combat deck, in some people's opinion (not mine)."

TS is not much more useful than FoD. FoD is a more limited use card (as it
should be, as a Rare), and has a different use (to stack on stuff), but is not
inherrently less useful.

"Arguments for the errata: original card text could be read the way the
errata says, and the current errata is the current errata, and it's
not a broken card with the errata."

And as you pointed out, original intent is always a good idea. I would (and
do) argue that the original intent of the Jyhad card was for it to work the way
it does now.

LSJ wrote:
"I'm saying that VTES card text clearly says that Torn Signpost works
as a strike-granting effect. It is the errata to the card that makes
it work as a strength-setting effect."

And again, I disagree that this is clear. The card says:

"This vampire can inflict 2 hand damage as a strike for the remainder of
combat."

And a vampire without the card can inflict 1 hand damage as a strike for the
remainder of combat. And a vampire playing with 3 FoD can inflict 7 hand
damage as a strike for the remainder of combat. This does not necessarily mean
that the card was attempting to restrict the using vampire to a "Strike: 2 hand
damage". Any vampire that has 2 hand damage can inflict 2 hand damage as a
strike for the remainder of combat.

This is just a dumb semantics argument, true. I simply don't see how the
ambigious VTES text is in any way clear about TS being some sort of
unprecidented strike gaining effect.

superior gives a Dodge. There is no such thing as a non-strike Dodge.
There was such a thing as 'doing 2 hand damage'; all the 2 hand damage
vampires did it.) My interpretation of Jyhad text is that 'does' should
be read as 'has', which would clearly have been a resetting of the vamp's
base hand damage. (ie, they should have used 'has' but didn't because
they weren't thinking quite clearly enough.)

: If anything, the Jyhad text seems to be: "This vampire must strike

ability to strike with increased hand damage instead of relying on the
players' common-sense reading that the Signpost simply reset the playing

expected players to read it in the (natural, to my mind) 'resets hand
damage' fashion. (Sketchy, I know.)

: > supports the VTES card text. (that is, the VTES text appears to me to

: > that the VTES text was simply wrong.)

: Tom didn't say that he was overturning anything - he may simply have

Which would be a good thing to base it on. ;-)

clear in terms of how the card works (I know you disagree here, but go with

"It is "more useful" when viewed in whole, cost included. How many times do you
see FoD used at all?"

FoD is used all the time. The reason it isn't seen that much is because it is
Rare, and thus hard to get. The Brujah don't need to use FoD, as they have
Celerity. However, the Nosferatu, Giovanni, and Lasombra need to stack FoD on
top of TS to be able to compete with the Brujah in terms of combat
effectiveness. If you are playing the Brujah, you don't need FoD. Otherwise
you do. If TS is changed from the way it currently works, this will become
even more apparent.

Regardless, "It'll make FoD get used more often" (as is the implication here,
although I don't really think that you support this view in any way) is not a
justification for changing Torn Signpost. What cards would you need to change
to have, say, Psychic Veil used more often?

"The "as a strike" is obviously implied. Or do you suggest that the damage from
the Jyhad version would be done even if the vampire Dodged? (certainly a viable

interpretation, but just as clearly wrong -just like Read Interpretations
(superior) implies a strike)"

And again, I fail to see how the "as a strike" implication of this card
precludes the use of Undead Strength to augment this strike. A vampire with a
default hand damage of 1 can strike for 1 hand damage, just as if he had 2 hand
damage from TS and could strike for 2 hand damage. This does not, however,
prevent him from using US as well, becasue the 1 hand damage from the default
strike does not lock him into using this "strike" only. Only cards that say
"Strike:X" do this, or weapons by defenition. Torn Signpost is neither.

"If it was intended to alter base hand damage (now called "strength"), and all
templates in Jyhad agreed (which they don't), then it certainly should've
followed the Drawing Out the Beast's (superior) template and said: "this
vampire's hand damage is 2.""

This is correct. However, it doesn't follow _any_ template. There is plenty
of evidence to make the card slide either way. I believe the strongest
evidence is that the Jyhad version stands on one end of the spectrum and we
were given no indication that TS was intentionally changed for any reason with
the VTES wording.

"All "current" errata that changed original intent (as far as can be
determined) was reviewed by the RT, or should be. Indeed, it should've been at
the time it was issued (and likely was, if it was identified as "errata" at the
time)."

But the errata (?) on the VTES card was changing _back_ to original intent.
The VTES wording arguably (I don't deny this) changes the way TS works from the
Jyhad version. However, there was no evidence given that this was done
intentionally. Look at all the other cards/effects that were changed between
Jyhad and VTES:

-2 Damage/Hand Damage was changed to +1 damage on melee weapons/vampires.
-2 Bleed was changed to +1 bleed on vampires (and Pulse)
-Chainsaw and MotSB were omitted from the set.
-Paralyze was removed and Stake reworded.

All of these were changed for very specific and explained reasons. Torn
Signpost was not. Heck, remember the issue of The Duelist that came out around
this time? It had a card by card description of every changed card in the set.
Torn Signpost wasn't even on this list.

Can you give me some other examples of cards that were substantially changed in
effect between the Jyhad and VTES version that was not explained by rules
adjustments?

"VTES Card Text:
Only usable before range is determined. This vampire can inflict 2 hand damage

Looks like it makes perfect sense to me. This card gives me the option of a

hand strike (no melee weapons) with a base hand damage of 2. It also doesn't

strike. Neither of these two conditions prevent the striking vampire from also

and as such, when looked at in light of the far clearer Jyhad wording and its
effect on the game environment as a whole should be read to work in the same
way as the Jyhad wording does.

"Maybe not. Perhaps the card was never intended to be used with a melee
weapon. This nonsense about Gangrels marking their territory is a load of
crap. Either way, the VTES version makes more sense to me."

The melee weapon aspect of this card is so much less an issue than its use as a
basic building block of an entire strategy. It gives you a bigger hand damage,
and melee weapons do damage based on your hand damage. FoD does the same
thing. Do you disagree that FoD should make melee weapons do more damage also?

picture of a signpost where FoD does not?

"This is primarily why you don't want the errata to change. It will make your
"Weenies with Potence" deck less viable in its current state and will require
it to be re-worked. A lot of others had the same problems on a grander scale
with 7/7."

should be changed because:

B) It will increase the dependeance of Potence decks on Rare cards.
C) I don't believe that the VTES wording is clear enough to make a definitive
statement as to what the editor who chose to re-write the VTES version was
trying to do. As this is the case, and we have no definitive statements from
the designers as to why the wording was changed, I don't think that there is
any reason to assume that they intentonally meant to change the way the card
works.

As to my personal feelings on the subject, making Pulled Fangs do non aggro
damage also made my various combat decks much weaker, yet I am a great
supporter of this change.

"*raises eyebrow* A stackable card is less usable? With the current errata,
using 1 FoD is the same as a TS...but costs a blood. Multiple FoDs can jack the
dmg waaay up"

I'm not quite sure who you are arging with here. My statement that you wrote
this in response to was saying "FoD is not inherrently less useful than TS", as
LSJ claimed that it was.
